To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hypomethylation of DNA in the promoter regions of several genes is a feature of hepatocellular carcinomas and that this hypomethylation is detectable by HRM analysis in clinical samples.
hypomethylated DNA regions of the FCRL1, GPM6B and MAGEA12 promoters are useful for diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinomas.
we have identified three DNA hypomethylations that distinguish liver cancer from normal liver tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and validation of biomarkers for liver cancers.
the development of DNA methylation biomarkers for early detection and diagnosis of liver cancer, which is the second leading cause of cancer-related death.
the discovery and validation of biomarkers that could be used for early detection of HCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present work has identified a set of DNA hypomethylations that can be used as diagnostic markers for HCC.
the present study is the first to demonstrate that hypomethylated DNA regions can serve as candidate biomarkers in cancer diagnostics.
the identified biomarkers differentiated liver cancers from normal adjacent liver in the Shanghai area and chronic hepatitis in another cohort.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypomethylated markers are as important for diagnosis of cancer as hypermethylated markers.
hypomethylation of DNA in cancer can be a diagnostic tool.
we have discovered and validated a panel of biomarkers for HCC that can be easily applied in clinical settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hypomethylation of cancer genes can be used as a biomarker in HCC and other solid tumors.
the use of HRM for methylation analysis is a simple, fast, and cost-effective approach to identify biomarkers that can be translated into the clinic.
the use of HRM as a diagnostic tool for DNA methylation in clinical samples is a feasible approach that can be used for the identification of biomarkers for solid tumors.
